samples.question: This page carries one black line figure and several coloured decorations. Only the black figure and the red stretch drawn inside it matter; blue, green, grey, purple and orange marks are decoration and never count. The black figure is a single thread: every black stroke in it is joined to the rest, and one short stretch of that thread is painted red instead of black, so the red stretch is a piece of the thread and not a separate object. Exactly one white pocket is fully enclosed by the thread as drawn. Now imagine cutting the red stretch out of the thread and leaving nothing behind in its place, while every black stroke stays exactly where it is. A white pocket counts as enclosed only when you cannot leave it and reach the outside of the page without crossing a black stroke. After that cut, is at least one white pocket still fully enclosed by the black strokes? Answer yes or no.
